newsitem.title: UK: UK to review arms export licenCe policy.
newsitem.headline: UK to review arms export licenCe policy.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday it would carry out an urgent review of the criteria used in considering licence applications for the export of conventional arms.
Officials from a number of government departments have been tasked to draw up a paper for ministers to consider, the Foreign Office said in a statement.

The statement said the government supported a strong British defence industry but was also committed to ensuring that export licences were not issued for the sale of arms to regimes that might use them for internal repression or international aggression.
It would also not permit the sale of weapons in circumstances where this might intensify or prolong existing armed conflict or where these weapons might be used to abuse human rights.

On Wednesday, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said he would ban the manufacture, export and import of anti-personnel land mines. Cook, in office since the May 1 election, has said he would place human rights at the heart of British foreign policy.
